cards.text: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, is waging war against Judah. So Zedekiah, king of Judah, sends two men to the prophet Jeremiah: Pashhur son of Malchijah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah. They've come with a request.

cards.question: With Babylon at war against them, what do Zedekiah's men ask Jeremiah to do?

answers.text: Inquire of the LORD for them
Make peace with Babylon for them
Lead the army out for them

cards.question: Zedekiah's men hope the LORD will do something like all His past ___, so Nebuchadnezzar will pull back.

cards.text: Jeremiah answers with a message for Zedekiah from the LORD, the God of Israel. Friend, it's like when my junk drawer rattled open and I thought, THIS is it, back to the counter… and it was somebody looking for tape.

cards.question: Zedekiah's army is out fighting Babylon. What does the LORD say He will turn against them?

answers.text: The weapons in their own hands
The walls of their own city
The horses in their own stables

cards.question: The LORD says He Himself will fight for Zedekiah against Babylon.

cards.text: The LORD says He will strike down the people of the city, both man and beast. They will die in a terrible plague.

cards.question: After the plague, the LORD says He will hand Zedekiah, his officers and the survivors over to Nebuchadnezzar. Nebuchadnezzar will show them pity.

cards.text: Then a message for the people. The LORD says, 'Behold, I set before you the way of life and the way of death.' Two roads, friend, and NO third one marked 'I'll get back to You.'

cards.question: With the Chaldeans besieging the city, who does the LORD say will live?
The LORD says He has set His face against the city and will hand it to the king of Babylon. What will that king do to it?

cards.text: Next, the LORD has a word for the royal family, the house of David. And friend, this job comes with an alarm clock and NO snooze button.

cards.question: Every morning, the house of David is told to administer ___ and rescue the victim of robbery from his oppressor.
If the house of David doesn't do this, the LORD says His wrath will burn like fire with no one to put it out.

cards.text: Then the LORD says He is against the ones who live above the valley, atop the rocky plateau. Friend, I spent years at the bottom of a junk drawer, so living up high sounds AMAZING to me.

cards.question: Up on that rocky plateau, what do they say about themselves?

answers.text: No one can come against us
The LORD will always protect us
Egypt will come to save us

cards.text: The LORD says He will punish them as their deeds deserve, with a fire in their forest that consumes everything around them. So much for "Who can come against us?"

Now the LORD sends Jeremiah down to the palace of the king of Judah, who sits on David's throne, with a word for the king, his officials and his people. Jeremiah's making a house call, friend, and the house is a PALACE.
Sound familiar? Administer justice and righteousness, and rescue the victim of robbery from the hand of his oppressor.

cards.question: The LORD also tells the king to do no wrong or violence to certain people. Who are they?

answers.text: Foreigners and the fatherless and widows

cards.text: And one more: "Do not shed innocent blood in this place." Then the LORD gives the king a big IF.

cards.question: If the king carries out these commands, kings who sit on David's throne will enter the palace gates riding on chariots and horses.

cards.text: Then the other side of that IF. The LORD swears by Himself, and friend, there's nobody higher to swear by.

cards.question: If the king doesn't obey, what does the LORD swear this palace will become?

cards.text: The LORD tells the king's house it is "like Gilead to Me, like the summit of Lebanon." A MOUNTAINTOP, friend. Nobody ever called me a mountaintop. Best I ever got was "huh, it still works."

cards.question: Even so, the LORD says He will turn the king's house into a desert, like cities where no one lives.
The LORD will appoint destroyers who cut down the choicest ___ of the king's house and throw them into the ___.

cards.text: Then many nations pass by the city and ask one another, 'Why has the LORD done such a thing to this great city?'

cards.question: When the nations ask why the LORD did this to the great city, what answer do people give?

answers.text: They forsook the LORD's covenant and served other gods
Their king lost a war to a stronger king
Their walls were built too low to hold back an army

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 8 quotes "like Gilead to Me, like the summit of Lebanon.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The drawer joke doesn't line up with what the card tells. The card's only fact is that Jeremiah answers with a message from the LORD. The joke is about hoping for rescue and getting a letdown, but the card never restates the men's hope for wonders, and the message hasn't been shown to be bad yet. 'It's like when…' has nothing on the card to compare to, so the baker has to work out the connection.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'Zedekiah's army is out fighting Babylon' suggests the army is outside the city. In Jeremiah 21:4 it is the Chaldeans who besiege the city 'outside the wall', and Zedekiah's people are fighting from inside the besieged city.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: 'If the house of David doesn't do this' uses 'this' to point back to card 13, which is no longer on screen. The question should say what the house of David must do (administer justice every morning and rescue the victim of robbery).

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'Up on that rocky plateau, what do they say about themselves?' points back to card 15 with 'that' and 'they'. The question never says who is speaking: the ones who dwell above the valley, whom the LORD says He is against.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'If the king carries out these commands' points back to cards 2 through 4, which are no longer on screen. The question should briefly say what the commands are, such as justice, rescuing the oppressed and not shedding innocent blood.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'There's nobody higher to swear by' states a Bible fact from Hebrews 6:13 ('since He had no one greater to swear by, He swore by Himself') without giving its reference.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: 'Then many nations pass by the city and ask one another' tells a prediction as if it were happening now. In Jeremiah 22:8 it is the LORD saying that many nations will pass by. The card should keep it as part of what the LORD says will happen.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
